name: Chin-Up (Weighted)
instructions: Hang from a bar with a supinated (palms toward you) grip at shoulder width, with a weight belt or dumbbell between your feet.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Pull your chin above the bar by driving your elbows toward your ribs.
Lower under control to a full hang.
cues: Full hang to chin over bar
longevityNotes: Pulling strength balances all the forward-reaching of daily life and protects the shoulders and upper back. A strong back is one of the best predictors of staying active and independent.
overview: A chin-up with added load to progress upper-body pulling strength.

sources.title: Original to the LIFT knowledge base

attribution: Original prose written for the LIFT knowledge base (CC BY 4.0).
commonMistakes: Loading before you can do strict bodyweight reps
safetyNotes: Be able to do 8 to 10 strict bodyweight chin-ups first; stop if elbows or shoulders hurt.
